chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, altogether, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Abdul Samad ibn Basheer, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said, 'May Allah keep you well. The one who loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him, and the one who hates meeting Allah, Allah hates to meet him.' He said: 'Yes.' I said, 'By Allah, we indeed dislike death.' So he said: 'That is not where you are going with it. Rather, that is at the time of witnessing (death), when he sees what he loves, so there is nothing more beloved to him than proceeding (to meet Allah), and Allah the Exalted loves to meet him, and he loves to meet Allah at that time. And when he sees what he dislikes, so there is nothing more hateful to him than meeting Allah, and Allah hates to meet him.'
ai.seo_question: Why do believers dislike death if they love meeting Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi resolves the apparent tension between the general human aversion to death and the spiritual ideal of longing for the Divine Meeting (Liqa' Allah) by distinguishing between the physical act of dying and the metaphysical moment of encounter. In Shia exegesis, this 'meeting' is not merely the cessation of life but the unveiling of one's spiritual state, where the believer's love for Allah transforms the fear of death into eager anticipation of witnessing the Divine Presence. This concept underscores the Shia emphasis on the transformative power of faith at the hour of death, linking inner spiritual reality with the external event of passing.
